content.title: What are Polymers?
content.description: Polymers are high molecular weight macromolecules formed by the repeated linking of small molecules called monomers through chemical reactions known as polymerization.

content.content: Polymers are widely used in engineering, medicine, packaging, textiles, automobiles, electronics, and construction due to their lightweight nature, strength, flexibility, and resistance to chemicals. Both natural and synthetic polymers play an important role in daily life.

content.title: Did You Know?
content.content: The word 'polymer' comes from the Greek words 'poly' meaning many and 'mer' meaning parts.
Definition of Polymer
A polymer is a giant molecule consisting of a large number of repeating structural units called monomers. These monomers are chemically bonded together to form long molecular chains.
Classification of Polymers
Polymers can be classified based on their source, structure, and method of polymerization.
Polymerization
Polymerization is the chemical process in which a large number of monomer molecules combine to form a polymer. The two major types are Addition Polymerization and Condensation Polymerization.
Addition Polymerization

In addition polymerization, unsaturated monomers containing double bonds combine without the elimination of any small molecule. It generally proceeds through a free radical mechanism involving initiation, propagation, and termination.

content.title: Free Radical Addition Polymerization
content.description: Free radicals initiate the reaction by opening the double bond of monomers, leading to chain growth until termination occurs.

content.content: Condensation Polymerization
In condensation polymerization, two or more different monomers react with the elimination of small molecules such as water, ammonia, or methanol to form polymers.
Nylon 6:6

Nylon 6:6 is a condensation polymer produced by the reaction of hexamethylene diamine and adipic acid with the elimination of water molecules. It possesses high strength, toughness, and excellent wear resistance.

content.title: Applications of Nylon 6:6
content.content: Used in gears, bearings, ropes, fishing nets, tyre cords, textile fibers, engineering plastics, and machine parts.
Terylene
Terylene (PET) is a polyester formed by the condensation reaction between ethylene glycol and terephthalic acid. It has high tensile strength, good chemical resistance, and dimensional stability.

content.title: Applications of Terylene
content.content: Used in textile fibers, PET bottles, films, packaging materials, seat belts, and industrial fabrics.
Comparison of Polymerization Methods
Advantages of Polymers

items.question: Light Weight
items.answer: Polymers are much lighter than metals, making them ideal for engineering applications.

items.question: Chemical Resistance
items.answer: Most polymers resist acids, alkalis, and corrosion.

items.question: Easy Processing
items.answer: They can be easily molded into different shapes and sizes.

items.question: Wide Applications
items.answer: Used in packaging, automobiles, electrical insulation, medicine, textiles, and aerospace.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Polymers are formed from repeating monomer units.
Polymerization is of two types: addition and condensation.
Addition polymerization does not eliminate by-products.
Condensation polymerization eliminates small molecules like water.
Nylon 6:6 is formed from adipic acid and hexamethylene diamine.
Terylene is a polyester formed from ethylene glycol and terephthalic acid.
